problem: The US band is given as 5.85–5.925 GHz without noting the 2020 FCC reallocation, in which the lower 45 MHz went to unlicensed use, so the figure is out of date for a student reading current material.
fix: Say that the original US DSRC band was 5.850–5.925 GHz, and that after the 2020 FCC order only the upper part, 5.895–5.925 GHz, is kept for vehicle communication; Europe still uses 5.855–5.925 GHz.

problem: The text lists IEEE 1609.2 security as one of the four 1609 standards, but the stack diagram leaves it out, so a student may think security sits outside the stack.
fix: Add a side note or an item for IEEE 1609.2 security (signed messages, certificates) spanning the 1609.3/1609.4 region of the stack.

problem: 1609.1 is a resource manager for applications, not a protocol layer in the stack, so calling all four 'IEEE 1609 layers' is loose and conflicts with the Figure.
fix: Ask for 'the four IEEE 1609 standards' rather than 'layers', and keep 1609.1 described as a resource manager.
